summary: The common Arch recipe compares both the complete sorted staged-file path population and the complete installed package inventory with stdin SHA256 values, reusing tooling already required for acquired-input verification. Standalone assignments under set -eu preserve failure from either hash command or input opening before equality is tested; a combined comparison expression can hide a failed command substitution. Source controls execute both literal comparison blocks and retain unequal-byte, missing-input, and failed-hash-with-matching-output cases. This source repair supplies no native image, trusted transaction closure, publication or installed acceptance. Native donor tooling still requires actual admission and verification.
title: Use existing checksum tooling for common image recipe equality guards
